You didn't forget that name. It was never lost.

Kevin Trudeau describes the moment you meet someone you've known for years and their name goes blank. You search and search, and it bugs you all day.

Then at two in the morning, two days later, the name pops into your head. Kevin's point is that this proves you never forgot it. It was in your memory the whole time, just misfiled.

When did a name come to you hours too late?

He offered free memory training to a whole school system. The answer was no.

Kevin Trudeau says that in the eighties he went to the Chicago school system and offered memory training to every teacher and student, free. It would have been a year of live events.

He saw it as a win-win: students would do better, and he would gain publicity. The offer was declined anyway.

Should schools teach students how to remember?

#ad #memory #success #education

He was told he had a learning disability. Then he met a researcher.

Kevin Trudeau says he was not born with a good memory, and in school he was told he had a learning disability. He struggled to remember information.

Then he met a researcher who worked with 35 blind children in Oklahoma. At the start of the study they recalled 15 percent of information. By the end it was 90 percent. The researcher's conclusion: if blind kids can improve, anyone can learn.

What label have you carried longer than you should?
